rendered: The solvent with the strongest hydrogen bonding in the paper is water. Its hydrogen-bonding strength is a δH value of 42.3[1] MPa^1/2 MPa, as plotted in Figure 6b[2]. For comparison, the other solvents in that comparison have lower δH values: glycerol 29.3[3] MPa^1/2 and diethylene glycol 20.7[4] MPa^1/2. Water is not used for delamination because the aluminum foil corrodes. Lithium leaching from the NMC cathode makes the water solution basic, and that corrosion of the aluminum would contaminate the NMC particles by forming Al(OH)3 precipitates on the cathode surfaces.[5][6][7][8]
